prompt:
I need the front end for Kettlefund. A disbursement tool for a volunteer-run neighborhood mutual-aid network's emergency fund, where the rotating fund committee approves small grants to neighbors and can void a payout before the volunteer treasurer sends it.

Who's using it: Dani Ruiz, a volunteer on this week's two-person fund committee. Dani works as a pharmacy tech, handles the fund on evenings, and has served on the committee about five times.

What they're doing right now: It is Wednesday evening and the November fund has $2,140 left with 18 requests waiting. Dani and the other reviewer, Abe, have split them. Dani has to decide which of their nine to fund and for how much, then commit each payout so the treasurer can send money Thursday at noon. Policy caps grants at $300 per household per quarter, and two of Dani's requesters already got money in October. Last week a payout was committed to the wrong payment handle and had to be voided, so Dani wants to be sure each commitment is right, knows that a committed payout can be voided only until the treasurer marks it sent, and that voiding returns the money to the pot.

What's in the system at this point: Fund balance: $2,140 available for November out of a $4,500 monthly pot from donations; $1,190 already sent this month across 6 grants, $1,170 committed but not yet sent across 5 grants (one voided last week for $150, now returned). 18 open requests, 9 assigned to Dani: each has a first name or alias, requested amount ($60–$400), need category (rent gap, utility shutoff, groceries, medication, transport to work), urgency (shutoff date of Nov 21 on one), how they want to be paid (Venmo, Cash App, Zelle, or a cash pickup at the church hall), the handle or pickup preference, and prior grants this quarter (two have $150 and $200). Committee rules: two reviewers must agree on any grant over $200; the treasurer sends Thursdays and Mondays at noon. Activity record of commits, voids and sends with who did each.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
